what: Serial double pendulum and physical bracing. Give a two-link pendulum one finite disturbance, then watch what keeps moving. Motor A moves a 16 mm-radius crank carrying the top pivot. The red 11L upper link has 80 mm between its two pivots; the blue 7L lower link extends 48 mm from its elbow to its end hole. Both joints use real frictionless pins. After the support motor returns and holds, neither link is commanded to follow a target. One motor gives the support a finite pulse. Two passive pendulum links keep moving after the support returns and holds. Compare their relative elbow angle with a real brace.
try: Choose Cascade in Robot Lab Examples. Its Blocks program loads automatically. Reset to the saved pose before each run; press Run to excite the support, then watch the free links.

Reset to the saved model before every fresh run. The program holds motor A first and admits only an encoder within ±1° of its saved datum. It verifies a 0.5 s startup hold, with no homing motion or encoder reset. The absolute unwrapped route is A=0 → 90 → 0° at 180 / 180°/s; declared holds after those legs are 0.3 / 0 s.

After its fresh arrival check at A=90°, the program holds motor A for 0.3 s and checks the target again before returning. The passive links remain free during this commanded outward hold; observing remains 0.

Watch stage 3 after the support returns: observing=1 marks the 12 s observation window. supportHeld=1 refers only to the held motor. The program repeatedly checks its fresh encoder error, with a 0.1 s wait between checks, and requires it within 0.5°. Independently check the moving top-pivot position relative to the actual frame before interpreting the pendulum motion.

Track upper_link and lower_link relative to the frame. Use the common physical hinge axis and unwrap their angles. Also calculate the elbow angle as lower angle minus upper angle. A moving lower tip alone does not show that the elbow is moving: both links could be swinging together as one rigid object.

Choose Cascade Control in Examples, reset it, and run the automatically loaded program. This control preserves every original placement and adds 6 real brace/pin parts. Compare the relative elbow motion while checking that the held support remains stationary and the remaining top pivot is still free. The original elbow_pin remains installed and may spin about its own axis; measure the two links, not that pin, to test the lock.

Read the observed angle ranges, elbow reversals and support motion from the supplied qualification JSON and trajectory CSV. Completion means the finite support route and observation have ended. The pendulum is allowed to continue moving afterward; no passive-output return or settling condition is imposed.
why: A motor can excite a passive mechanism without prescribing its later motion. Moving the top pivot changes the forces on the upper link; the elbow transmits forces between the two links. Once the support is held, gravity and inertia govern the two coupled angular coordinates, while the model’s declared damping dissipates motion. Holding motor A fixes the support input, not either free hinge. The physical brace removes relative rotation at the elbow, leaving one pendulum assembly hanging from the top pivot.
matters: Compare two serial passive joints with the collection’s separately suspended pendulums and elastically coupled pendulums. Cascade asks whether relative motion persists inside the chain while its support is held. The brace comparison tests that degree of freedom directly. Because its extra pieces also change mass and inertia, it is not a mass-matched test of an unchanged oscillation period. Angle traces alone do not measure energy transfer or establish chaotic behavior.
question: After motor A has returned to zero and holds, must the blue lower link stop? Which measurement distinguishes two-link motion from a single rigid pendulum? Predict what changes when the elbow brace is installed, and whether both versions must return their passive links to the saved pose before the program completes.
answer: The lower link can keep moving after the support motor stops. Measure the relative elbow angle, q₂−q₁, as well as each link’s angle relative to the frame. In the free model that difference can change and reverse while both links move. In the braced control it should remain approximately constant, although the combined assembly can still swing about the top pivot. Neither version needs to return its passive links to the initial pose or settle before completion. The recorded physical comparison determines the actual motion ranges and residuals.
further: Use actual link-body orientations and body-carried pivot points. Check hinge closure and held support motion separately from encoder arrival; successful motor commands are not proof that the passive chain moved correctly.

Separate the outward movement and commanded hold, the support-return correction, and the post-return observation. The outward hold changes the excitation timing while the links remain free; it is distinct from a dwell produced by a mechanism. Exclude the declared guard interval at the start of the measurement window if the qualification contract specifies one.

The 80 mm and 48 mm dimensions are pivot-to-pivot or pivot-to-end-hole spans, not the overall plastic lengths and not point-mass pendulum lengths. These beams have distributed mass, and the serial system has coupled coordinates; a single simple-pendulum period does not describe the whole machine.

Inspect the exact added control IDs in catalog-proposal.json and the assembly ledger. The elbow is locked by real parts; the control does not freeze a body in software or add an invisible joint. Its added mass and inertia remain part of the interpretation.

Keep the qualified geometry, motor route and operating envelope. Reset before repeating, rather than restarting the program while the links still swing. Different amplitudes, speeds, added bobs or friction pins require a new construction and operating-envelope check.
formula: Kinematic definitions: q₁ and q₂ are independently observed link angles about the common hinge axis; the relative elbow angle is Δ=q₂−q₁. In an ideal planar projection, tip−support = 80u(q₁)+48u(q₂) mm, where u(q) is the downward unit vector rotated through q in that plane. The two link lengths sum to 128 mm. This is a geometric relationship, not a time-history or energy prediction. In the saved straight brace control, Δ is constant; the one remaining pendulum angle may still vary.
